The candidate link A–D (dashed) has two common neighbors, both in the accent color. B shares the pair's community, so it counts twice; C does not, so it counts once. The card adds 2 + 1 for a score of 3.0." width="100%"} Soundarajan and Hopcroft (2012) refine the common-neighbor count using community membership: for two nodes in the same community, each common neighbor that is also in that community counts twice. Pairs in different communities get the plain count. The idea is that links are more likely inside communities, so shared in-community neighbors are stronger evidence. Communities come from a node attribute, such as the one written by `cmty_louvain()` or `cmty_leiden()`. The graph is treated as undirected and simple. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of `(u, v)` pairs to score. If `None` (default), every pair of non-adjacent nodes is scored. [community]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute holding community labels (default `"community"`). Every node must have it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v, score)` triples with node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, a node lacks the community attribute or does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pair costs one neighbor-set intersection. The scores match NetworkX's `cn_soundarajan_hopcroft`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A and D share the neighbors B and C, but only B is in their community, so the score is 2 + 1 = 3: ::: {#3a2e86a7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes( [("A", {"community": 0}), ("B", {"community": 0}), ("C", {"community": 1}), ("D", {"community": 0})] ) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) g.cn_soundarajan_hopcroft([("A", "D")])[0][2] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: :::
